$comment: Chassis dynos and their correction standards (BUILD_PROMPT 6.5), for normalising known-build sheets (src/sim/dyno-correction.ts). readingFactor: what the dyno reads for a car a Dynojet (inertia roller) reads 1.00 on, same car and correction; the model's wheel power is a Dynojet-type reading. Research: docs/research/part2b/dyno-normalisation.json.

sources.title: Road & Track (Matt Farah), "We Put 4 Dynos to the Test With a Ford Mustang Dark Horse" (syndicated, 2 Apr 2026)
sources.note: It was 74 degrees and sunny ... Fifth gear is the 1:1 ratio in the Dark Horse's Tremec, so all pulls were done in fifth. All four readings were calibrated using the same SAE weather correction factor. [Dynojet 248X 425.7 whp; Dynapack 430.9; SuperFlow AutoDyn 420.8; Mustang AWD 465, on a car Ford rates at 500 hp.]

readingFactor.note: The reference by definition. Check on the model's own chain: R&T's Dynojet 248X read 425.7 whp from a car rated 500 hp (0.851); the model's manual crank-to-wheel chain is 0.98 x 0.94 x 0.92 = 0.848.

sources.title: Dynojet, WinPEP 7 User Guide, part 98118103 v02 (08/2006)
sources.note: p. 2-2: 'Data can either be viewed as measured (“uncorrected”) or corrected to standard atmospheric conditions using WinPEP.' p. 7-8: 'Default Correction Factor — specifies the correction factor.' Figure 7-6 shows 'Default Correction Factor: SAE'.

sources.title: Dynojet University, "Understanding Dyno Correction Factors (SAE, STD, DIN) and Smoothing" (4 Jul 2025)
sources.note: SAE ... corrects the numbers to a standard of 29.235 inches of mercury (approximately 99 kPa) at 77°F (25°C) with 0% humidity. ... For a tuner, it's crucial to always correct your dyno runs to SAE.

defaultCorrection.method: No factory default is published. WinPEP 7's settings screenshot shows 'Default Correction Factor: SAE' and Dynojet tells tuners to always correct to SAE, so a sheet that doesn't say is taken as SAE. STD would read about 3-4 % higher.

readingFactor.method: Same-car comparisons disagree by machine and mode: DSPORT's rear-drive Supra 0.883 and 0.840, HP Academy's tutor 0.885-0.893 (12-13 % added to match), but R&T's rear-drive Dark Horse 1.092 on an AWD Mustang. 0.885, the middle of the rear-drive results, is used; expect about ±10 %.

sources.title: Mustang Dynamometer, PowerDyne PC user manual (2017-05-22)
sources.note: Use SAE Corrections: If you wish to have all data corrected per SAE J1349 (Jun90) (or your own custom standards), check this option.

defaultCorrection.method: PowerDyne offers SAE J1349 (Jun90) as its 'Use SAE Corrections' option; its factory state isn't stated, so an unstated Mustang sheet is taken as SAE.

sources.title: HP Academy forum, "Mainline vs Dynapack hp numbers"
sources.note: Andre Simon: 'From my own testing it seems that the mainline reads about 15-18% lower than Dynapack.' Orlando Bello: 'my DD also real like 15% lower than Dynojet'

readingFactor.method: Tuners' rules of thumb only: about 15 % below a Dynojet (a DD owner) and 'somewhat similar' to Mainline. Shootout classes move the same car's reading by about 15 %, so a DD sheet needs its class.

defaultCorrection.method: Dyno Dynamics' own correction modes (shootout, ATMC) are not documented publicly; SAE J1349 is assumed only so an unstated sheet has a reference air, and such sheets are not used for the calibration.

sources.note: Andre Simon: 'From my own testing it seems that the mainline reads about 15-18% lower than Dynapack.' Orlando Bello: 'my DD also real like 15% lower than Dynojet'

readingFactor.method: An HP Academy tutor who owns a Mainline and a Dynapack puts the Mainline 15-18 % below a Dynojet (and the same below a Dynapack); 0.835 is the middle. A Supra tuner in the research quotes x1.18 to convert Mainline to Dynojet (0.847). No controlled test was found.

defaultCorrection.method: Mainline's software offers several standards; the Mainline sheets found in the research print 'SAE J607', so an unstated one is taken as J607.
